correctness.rationale: Commutators are exactly two-by-two minors of the reduced coefficient vectors. Primitive rank-one matrices over any finite chain quotient factor as outer products and are counted by quotienting primitive factors by units. Valuation shells contribute the proved rank-one lift counts; deep entries contribute separately. Even/odd length sums collapse to the same two-pole formula. Stirling inversion gives each distinct clique coefficient and the scalar universal vertices give the noncentral graph. Ten direct tuple censuses, eight direct f-vector counts, nine isotropic submodule censuses, and 360 algebraic identity tests passed. Finite experiments are not general proof.

value.rationale: The result gives an entire canonical simultaneous-commutation moment sequence and clique f-vector for an infinite class of finite noncommutative algebras, not a special numerical slice. The exact two-pole form shows ring-structure invariance for all arities, and resolves intermediate clique sizes in connected nonfield commuting graphs. All parameters and characteristic-two cases are covered without appealing to unverified applications or significance.
